nodes.label: GooseOS Affine Matrix Game Screenshot
nodes.description: Screenshot of the affine matrix transformation game running inside a Win95-style window titled 'Goose.exe'. The game viewport is a white-bordered black rectangle centered in the window. A small white pixel-art goose/llama character is visible near the center of the viewport. Two 3x3 affine transformation matrices are displayed inside the viewport in monospace text: one on the lower-left and one on the lower-right. The matrices represent the current transformation state of the game. Outside the viewport (top-left of the window body) are three HUD stats: 'coordinates: -37, 37', 'time: 00:00:04.373', and 'matrices: 2'. Three red heart icons are displayed in the top-right corner of the window body, indicating the player has 3 lives remaining. The OS taskbar at the bottom shows a './start' button, mimicking the Win95 Start button. The desktop background is a blurred green field with blue sky, consistent with a Win95 aesthetic.

nodes.label: Player Character (Pixel-Art Goose/Llama)
nodes.description: A small white pixel-art character resembling a goose or llama, positioned near the center of the black game viewport. The sprite is minimal — roughly 10-15 pixels tall — consistent with a retro lo-fi visual style. It is the player-controlled entity navigating the affine transformation space.

nodes.label: Affine Transformation Matrix (Left)
nodes.description: A 3x3 affine transformation matrix displayed in monospace text in the lower-left area of the game viewport. Values read approximately: [[-1.41, 1.12, -7.00], [-1.45, -1.44, -39.00], [0.00, 0.00, 1.00]]. Displayed in orange/amber monospace font. Represents one of the two active transformation obstacles or waypoints in the game world.

nodes.label: Affine Transformation Matrix (Right)
nodes.description: A 3x3 affine transformation matrix displayed in monospace text in the lower-right area of the game viewport. Values read approximately: [[-0.38, -0.68, 15.00], [0.98, -0.54, 26.00], [0.00, 0.00, 1.00]]. Displayed in orange/amber monospace font. Represents the second active transformation matrix in the current game state.

nodes.label: HUD Stats Display (Coordinates, Time, Matrices)
nodes.source_location: top-left of window body, outside viewport
nodes.description: Three lines of HUD text displayed in small white monospace font outside the game viewport in the upper-left of the Win95 window body: 'coordinates: -37, 37' (player's current position in transformation space), 'time: 00:00:04.373' (elapsed game time showing precision to milliseconds), 'matrices: 2' (the count of active affine matrices currently present in the game). These metrics communicate the player's spatial state and game progression.

nodes.label: Lives Display (Heart Icons)
nodes.description: Three red heart icons arranged horizontally in the top-right corner of the Win95 window body (outside the game viewport). They indicate the player currently has 3 lives remaining. The heart design is simple and bold, consistent with the retro pixel-art aesthetic of the game.

nodes.label: Win95-Style Game Window (Goose.exe)
nodes.description: The entire game runs inside a Win95-style window with a blue title bar reading 'Goose.exe' and the standard minimize/maximize/close buttons (shown as box icons) in the top-right corner of the title bar. The window sits on a Win95-style desktop with a green-field-and-blue-sky wallpaper. A taskbar is visible at the bottom with a './start' button, a terminal-inspired twist on the classic Windows 'Start' button. The window is not maximized — it occupies most of the desktop area but leaves some desktop visible around it.

nodes.label: Game Viewport Canvas (Black Rectangle)
nodes.description: The game's rendering canvas is a solid black rectangle outlined with a thin white border, centered within the Win95 window. The black background provides high contrast for the white pixel-art character and the amber/orange matrix text. The canvas represents the affine transformation game world where all game objects and matrices are rendered.

nodes.label: Visual Style: Retro Win95 + Matrix Math Aesthetic
nodes.description: The game deliberately blends two retro aesthetics: (1) Win95 desktop UI chrome (title bar, taskbar, window decorations, classic wallpaper) and (2) a math/terminal aesthetic inside the viewport (black background, monospace matrix notation, pixel-art character). The orange/amber matrix text evokes old CRT terminal displays. The overall design communicates that the game's core mechanic is mathematical — affine transformations — while wrapping it in nostalgic desktop OS chrome for ironic/playful effect.

nodes.label: Core Game Mechanic: Affine Matrix Navigation
nodes.description: The game's core mechanic involves navigating a player character through a 2D space defined by affine transformation matrices. The 'matrices: 2' counter and two visible 3x3 matrices suggest that matrices appear as entities in the game world (obstacles, targets, or portals). The player's position is tracked as a 2D coordinate (-37, 37), and elapsed time is measured with millisecond precision. Interaction with matrices likely applies the transformation to the player's coordinate space, altering movement, orientation, or scale — a mechanic unique to the affine game concept described in the codebase.
